task.description: WF-02 Step 2c re-verification after rework iteration 1: the only change since the original Step 2c PASS is extracting the ranking CASE SQL literal into a @rank_case_sql module attribute (was duplicated inline in two functions, now defined once and referenced at both call sites via fragment(@rank_case_sql, ...)). Diff against origin/main (local main is stale, belongs to a different checkout).
acceptance_criteria: Confirm @rank_case_sql is a fixed compile-time module attribute (not derived from any runtime/user input)
Confirm fragment(@rank_case_sql, ...) at both call sites still has every ? placeholder bound to a column reference or ^-pinned value, same as before
Confirm no new SQL-injection surface was introduced by this refactor -- the SQL text itself is byte-identical to what was already reviewed, just relocated
Re-run mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors and confirm it exits 0

result.summary: Re-verification of rework iteration 1 (commit c1a4c2e). Confirmed via git diff fc59e80..c1a4c2e -- lib/letflow/definitions.ex that this is a pure mechanical refactor: the ranking CASE SQL text "CASE WHEN lower(?) = lower(?) THEN 3.0 WHEN ? ILIKE ? THEN 2.0 ELSE 1.0 END" was moved verbatim (byte-identical) from two inline fragment/1 first-argument literals into a single @rank_case_sql module attribute (definitions.ex:719), assigned directly as a literal string with no <>, #{} interpolation, or function-call construction -- confirmed a fixed compile-time literal by direct read. Both call sites, select_with_rank/3 (721-733) and order_by_rank/3 (735-749), reference it as fragment(@rank_case_sql, d.name, ^search_query, d.name, ^pattern) -- identical placeholder bindings (2 column refs, 2 ^-pinned values) to the pre-refactor inline calls; no new ? placeholder, no new binding, no new SQL text introduced. The already-reviewed where_search_match/2 fragment ("? ILIKE ? OR ? ILIKE ?", line 698) is untouched by this diff. No new injection surface. mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors exits 0 (verified via $? immediately after the command, not through a pipe). All four acceptance criteria met; original Step 2c PASS stands unchanged for the rest of search/2.
